title: Net Salary Calculator: Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay with Casual Loading and Super
description: Use our net salary calculator to turn your hourly rate into annual, fortnightly and weekly pay. Includes casual loading, super on top and 2026–27 tax.
salarySummary: For a 38‑hour week, your annual gross pay is your hourly rate multiplied by 38 then by 52, with casual loading and super added on top.

faqs.q: How do I calculate my annual salary from an hourly rate?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then by 52 weeks. For a standard full‑time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. This gives your annual gross pay before tax and super. If you are a casual employee, add 25% casual loading to your base rate before doing the calculation. Superannuation is then paid on top of your ordinary earnings at 12%.

faqs.q: What is casual loading and how does it affect my pay?
faqs.a: Casual loading is an extra 25% paid on top of the base hourly rate to compensate casual employees for not receiving paid leave or other entitlements. The National Minimum Wage for casuals from 1 July 2026 is $33.05 per hour (base $26.44 plus 25% loading). When using a net salary calculator, you should enter your base rate and let the calculator add the loading – never enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

faqs.q: Is superannuation included in my hourly rate or paid on top?
faqs.a: Super is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The Super Guarantee is 12% of your gross pay (up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year). For example, if your annual ordinary earnings are $50,000, your employer must contribute an extra $6,000 to your super fund. This is not deducted from your take‑home pay.

## How to Use a Net Salary Calculator for Australian Pay

A **net salary calculator** helps you see what your hourly rate means as annual, fortnightly or weekly pay – and what you’ll take home after tax and Medicare. This guide explains the maths, the rules for casual loading, and how super is paid on top.

### The Basic Formula: Hourly × Hours × 52

Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52 weeks. For a standard full‑time week of 38 hours, that’s:

**Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52**

This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances or salary sacrifice. It’s a starting point for comparing offers or checking your own pay.
